method.floor_definition: unweighted mean of qualifying surfaces' own per-dimension means, within a (string_type, dimension) cell -- never averaged across types or dimensions. Matches reference/netflix-index-v1-method.md's floor concept.
method.qualification_bar: n >= 5 non-suppressed items for that specific (surface, string_type, dimension) cell (per-dimension n, since suppression differs by dimension -- not the cell's raw item count).
method.comparison: Welch's t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, equal_var=False) of the qualifying surface's own per-item scores vs. the pooled per-item scores of the OTHER qualifying surfaces in the same cell, plus Cohen's d with the pooled SD.
method.correction: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (scipy.stats.false_discovery_control, method='bh'), applied once across every surface-vs-rest comparison with status=='tested' in the whole run.
method.mde: Normal-approximation minimum detectable effect per comparison, alpha=0.05 two-sided, power=0.80: d_min = (z_a/2 + z_power) * sqrt(1/n_self + 1/n_rest).

verdicts.extends: BH-adjusted p < 0.05 AND |Cohen's d| >= 0.5 AND this comparison's own MDE <= 0.5 (adequately powered). A surface must clear significance, effect size, AND power discipline together -- none alone is sufficient.
verdicts.within_floor: adequately powered (MDE <= 0.5) but not significant/not a medium effect -- a real, informative null.
verdicts.underpowered: this comparison's own MDE > 0.5 -- the achieved n could not have reliably found a medium effect even if one existed, regardless of what the raw p-value says.
verdicts.insufficient_data: n < 5 for this surface in this cell (reason: own_n_below_5), OR this surface qualifies but every other Netflix surface in this cell does not, leaving no rest-group to compare against (reason: no_rest_group_available).

method.reused_from: plays/papers/two-brands/scripts/score.py (cohens_d_pooled, minimum_detectable_effect formulas) and stats.md (test choice, FDR discipline, MDE formula, alpha/power). This is a new analysis (Netflix surface vs. pooled other Netflix surfaces), not a rerun of the two-brands Netflix-vs-Discord comparisons -- its FDR family is separate and corrected on its own.
